findings.title: Failed device tag stays cached and bypasses limit
findings.body: In pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go tagDeviceUI caches the device key with SetDefault before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice and never evicts on failure. When the device limit is reached the first request returns ErrDeviceLimitReached and client.go blocks auth, but the key remains in localCache for 29 minutes. The next request from the same rejected device hits the cache early-return nil and authenticates successfully. Consequence: the limit blocks only one request per TTL and is effectively unenforced on retry.

findings.title: Count-then-insert race allows exceeding device limit
findings.body: In pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go CreateOrUpdateDevice does CountDevices in one DB session and then INSERT or updateDevice in a second session with no transaction or lock. Concurrent anonymous requests can both observe count < deviceLimit and both insert. Consequence: under concurrent load the stored device count can overshoot the configured limit, so the limit is not strictly enforced.

findings.title: Zero rows affected misclassified as limit reached on MySQL
findings.body: In pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go updateDevice maps rowsAffected==0 to ErrDeviceLimitReached. On MySQL an UPDATE that matches a row but does not change any column values reports 0 rows affected. An existing active device re-tagging with the same IP/user-agent within the same second-precision updated_at will therefore be rejected as over-limit. Consequence: legitimate returning anonymous devices are blocked when the limit is reached.

findings.title: Provider signature change breaks wiring and custom stores
findings.body: In pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go ProvideAnonymousDeviceService was changed from taking anonStore AnonStore to taking sqlStore db.DB and constructing the store internally with cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit, and ProvideAnonDBStore now requires a deviceLimit int64. No wire_gen update is included and callers can no longer inject a custom AnonStore for testing or enterprise overrides. Consequence: existing server wiring and any external caller using the old provider signatures fails to compile.

findings.title: No test that existing device still updates after limit
findings.body: In pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database_test.go TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only checks that a second distinct device gets ErrDeviceLimitReached. It never checks that updating the first existing device after the limit is reached still succeeds via the updateDevice path. Consequence: the core guarantee that returning devices remain allowed to authenticate when the limit is reached is untested and regressions will go unnoticed.
